title: Hammurabi law 199, in King's English, prices a slave's eye at half the slave's value
summary: King's Hammurabi prices a slave's eye or bone at half the slave's value.
body: Law 199 in the same translation says that if he put out the eye of a man's slave, or break the bone of a man's slave, he shall pay one-half of its value. The code on this page does not give the slave the same bodily penalty it gives a man of equal status in law 196. The wording on the page includes: "eye of a freed man, or break the bone of a freed man, he shall pay one gold mina. 199. If he put out the eye of a man's slave, or break the bone of a man's slave, he shall pay one-half of its value. 200. If a man knock out the teeth of his equal, his teeth shall be knocked out. [ A tooth for a tooth ] 201. If he knock out the teeth of a freed man, he shall pay one-third of a gold".
